# krun

<!-- Generated by helm-docs through make generate. Edit README.md.gotmpl and values.yaml, not README.md. -->

Chart version: 0.0.0. App version: 0.0.0.

krun runs containerized functions as Kubernetes Jobs. This source chart supports
Postgres gateway/scheduler Deployments or one embedded SQLite StatefulSet with
an optional Litestream restore/replication sidecar. It does not provision a
database, credentials, object-storage bucket, Function resources or a Gateway.

This reference documents current templates, not a completed production release.
Chart-installed serving, CNI/data-plane, upgrade and rollback acceptance is
exercised by `make e2e` in P7.6; PodMonitor/PrometheusRule rendering and the complete
Phase 7 gate remain P7.7. The `metrics.*` values are reserved until that implementation.

## Prerequisites and Secret references

- Helm 4 and Kubernetes 1.33 or newer, with a CNI that actually enforces
  NetworkPolicy. Satisfying the API version alone does not prove isolation.
- Pre-create the release namespace and label it
  `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted`; the chart does not label it.
  Use a separate jobs namespace and select the cluster's real DNS pods.
- Provide `apiKeys.existingSecret` in the release namespace, with key
  `keys.yaml`. Postgres mode also requires `db.postgres.existingSecret` with
  key `dsn`, plus operator-managed Postgres 16 or newer. The chart uses Secret
  references only. Do not put credential material in values or command lines.
- With `jobsNamespace.create=false`, pre-provision the jobs namespace, restricted
  PSA labels, default-deny/DNS/internal-gateway/storage NetworkPolicies,
  LimitRange and ResourceQuota. Compare its Pod budget with `config.maxRunning`
  yourself. The job ServiceAccount, RBAC and enabled digest admission policy
  still render. Author/viewer Roles are deliberately not bound automatically.
- S3 settings are wired into both serving processes when `objectStorage.enabled`
  is true. Provide an operator-provisioned bucket, endpoint, signing region and
  release-namespace Secret with `accessKey` and `secretKey`. There is
  no runtime region default: partial S3 configuration with region omitted fails
  `ConfigInvalid(KRUN_S3_REGION)`. Explicit storage egress peers must match actual
  destinations; an empty peer list permits none. S3 account credentials never
  enter migration, restore, Litestream or function containers; function uploads
  use only their existing per-Run signed capability.
- Webhook host/CIDR allowlists are wired into gateway validation and scheduler
  delivery when `webhooks.allowedHosts` is nonempty. Provide an existing
  release-namespace Secret with key `secret`, containing comma-separated
  rotation signing keys. Only the scheduler receives that signing Secret
  reference. Empty hosts disable chart-configured delivery without injecting
  unused allowlists or credentials. No platform egress grants are added.

## Inspect and install from source

Run from the repository root. These offline examples validate/render the chart;
Secret names are references, not generated credentials. Pick an available,
trusted platform image before a real installation; `0.0.0` is development
metadata, not evidence that an image has been published.

```sh
helm lint deploy/helm/krun --strict \
  --set apiKeys.existingSecret=krun-test-docs-keys \
  --set db.postgres.existingSecret=krun-test-docs-postgres
helm template krun-test-docs deploy/helm/krun \
  --namespace krun-test-docs-platform \
  --set apiKeys.existingSecret=krun-test-docs-keys \
  --set db.postgres.existingSecret=krun-test-docs-postgres \
  --set jobsNamespace.name=krun-test-docs-jobs
helm template krun-test-docs deploy/helm/krun \
  --namespace krun-test-docs-platform \
  --set db.mode=embedded --set gateway.replicas=1 --set scheduler.replicas=1 \
  --set apiKeys.existingSecret=krun-test-docs-keys \
  --set jobsNamespace.name=krun-test-docs-jobs
```

For an actual operator-approved target, prepare the prerequisites above and a
private values file containing Secret names, not their contents. Then use
`helm install <release> deploy/helm/krun --namespace <release-namespace> --values <values-file>`.
Do not use `--create-namespace` as a substitute for the release namespace's PSA
label or jobs-namespace prerequisites. No installation is performed by
`make generate`.

Postgres migration is a pre-install/pre-upgrade hook, completed before serving
pods roll out. Embedded mode requires both replica values at most one; its
shared PVC is mounted at `/data`, with SQLite at `/data/krun.db`; Deployments
are not rendered.
Litestream requires a digest-pinned image and an existing Secret containing
`LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID` and `LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`. Restore starts first, the native replication sidecar starts next, then migrate
completes before the serving containers start.
Expect brief downtime during embedded rollout; this is not an HA database.

## Ownership, upgrade and uninstall

The Function CRD is templated into the Helm release, not a `crds/` special-case
file. With `crds.install=false`, apply `deploy/crds/functions.krun.io.yaml`
yourself before every install or upgrade. `crds.keep=true` retains the CRD on
uninstall; deleting it deletes every Function. A kept CRD or jobs namespace
retains the old release's Helm ownership annotations: reinstall with the same
release name/namespace, or explicitly re-annotate ownership as described in
[SPEC section 13](../../../SPEC.md#13-deployment).
For adoption by a different release, first verify that no other release still
owns these resources, then replace the uppercase placeholders below with the
intended names and explicitly transfer the retained resources:

```text
kubectl annotate crd functions.krun.io meta.helm.sh/release-name=RELEASE meta.helm.sh/release-namespace=PLATFORM_NAMESPACE --overwrite
kubectl annotate namespace JOBS_NAMESPACE meta.helm.sh/release-name=RELEASE meta.helm.sh/release-namespace=PLATFORM_NAMESPACE --overwrite
```

The namespace annotation is needed only when that namespace was chart-managed
and kept. With `crds.install=false`, the operator-managed CRD command is
`kubectl apply -f deploy/crds/functions.krun.io.yaml`; run it before each install
or upgrade. Do not delete the CRD just to clear its old Helm ownership.

`jobsNamespace.keep=true` keeps the namespace, its Secrets and in-flight Jobs,
not the chart's LimitRange, ResourceQuota or NetworkPolicies. Reinstall requires
restoring those controls before allowing untrusted Jobs. Embedded PVC data has
its own lifecycle; do not assume `helm uninstall` is a database backup.

Use `helm upgrade` for changes. Migrations are forward-only expand/contract;
one-minor `helm rollback` compatibility is the specified policy. P7.6 exercises
a configuration-only upgrade and rollback to revision 1 with the current-source
image; it does not prove compatibility of future different binary releases.
Keep scheduler downtime below
`config.ttlAfterFinished` so finished Job observations remain available.
See [operations](../../../docs/OPERATIONS.md) for migration, recovery, retained
ownership and first checks. Local chart-installed acceptance is separate from
independent review, hosted delivery, P7.7 monitoring and the full Phase 7 gate.

## Optional integrations and isolation

- `gatewayApi.httpRoute.enabled` creates one Gateway API v1 HTTPRoute to the
  release's public Service on 8080 only. Install compatible Gateway API CRDs and
  a controller yourself, configure the target Gateway's `allowedRoutes`, and
  provide `parentRefs` for attachment. Empty references deliberately attach to
  nothing. The chart creates no Gateway, GatewayClass or ReferenceGrant.
  Configure TLS and long-wait/SSE timeouts on the external Gateway/controller;
  a rendered or API-admitted route is not proof of routed traffic.
- A nonempty `observability.otlpEndpoint` enables OTLP/HTTP trace export from
  serving gateway/scheduler containers with the string-preserved sampling ratio
  (including zero). Empty drops traces. Migration/restore/Litestream/function
  containers do not receive these optional settings.
- `jobsNamespace.userNamespaces=true` sets `hostUsers: false` on function pods
  through the scheduler, never on platform pods. Ensure compatible Kubernetes,
  CRI, kernel and ID-mapped storage support; API admission is not proof of
  successful function execution under user namespaces.
- Jobs policies default-deny ingress and egress, permitting only configured DNS,
  the release gateway on 8081, enabled storage peers/port and explicit extra
  CIDRs. Broad `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0` entries defeat that isolation. The public
  Service and HTTPRoute never expose 8081 or admin ports. Platform ingress
  policies do not grant platform egress; `networkPolicy.metricsFrom={}` permits
  admin scraping from all namespaces, not no namespaces.
